title: Transaction Monitoring System Overhaul for Regional Bank
challenge: A mid-sized regional bank was struggling with a legacy transaction monitoring platform that generated an overwhelming volume of false-positive alerts, creating alert fatigue among analysts and delaying detection of genuinely suspicious activity. Regulators had flagged concerns after a routine examination.
solution: We rebuilt the alerting logic from the ground up, introducing tiered risk scoring, behavior-based typologies, and machine-learning-assisted pattern recognition. Governance workflows were redesigned to route higher-risk alerts to senior investigators, and analyst training was updated to align with the new methodology.
results: Within nine months the bank cut false-positive rates by nearly two-thirds while surfacing significantly more true suspicious activity reports. The updated framework passed its next regulatory examination without findings and freed analyst capacity for higher-value investigative work.

title: Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment for Money Services Business
challenge: A cross-border money services business needed a defensible counter-financing-of-terrorism (CFT) risk assessment covering more than forty remittance corridors, including several higher-risk jurisdictions. Their existing methodology relied on outdated typologies and lacked evidentiary support.
solution: Our team designed a corridor-level CFT risk model incorporating current FATF typologies, sanctions exposure, customer behavior indicators, and jurisdictional risk data. We documented the methodology in a regulator-ready evidence pack and delivered a remediation roadmap for higher-risk corridors.
results: The refreshed assessment was accepted by the client's supervisory authority as a substantial improvement and became the operating baseline for enhanced due diligence programs in high-risk corridors.

title: Real-Time Card Fraud Detection Uplift for Digital Wallet
challenge: A fast-growing digital wallet provider was seeing a sharp rise in card-not-present fraud, driven by account-takeover attacks and social-engineering scams. Existing rules-based defenses could not keep pace with rapidly evolving attacker behavior.
solution: We layered a behavioral biometrics signal, device intelligence, and a real-time scoring engine on top of the existing rules stack. Response playbooks were rewritten to enable step-up authentication and dynamic velocity limits without adding friction to legitimate customers.
results: Chargeback rates fell sharply within one quarter, customer complaints about false declines dropped, and net authorized-push-payment fraud losses were materially reduced.

title: Enterprise-Wide AML Risk Assessment for Universal Bank
challenge: A universal bank operating across retail, corporate, and private banking lines needed a unified enterprise-wide AML risk assessment. Prior efforts had produced siloed, inconsistent scoring and were difficult to defend to the group's board risk committee.
solution: We built a single, consistent risk assessment methodology covering customer, product, geography, and channel factors, and calibrated it against internal loss data and peer benchmarks. A board-level dashboard translated technical output into decision-useful narrative for governance forums.
results: The new methodology gave leadership a shared view of residual AML risk across business lines, informed the group's control investment priorities, and became the basis for the following year's supervisory dialogue.

title: Sanctions Screening Remediation for Global Payments Provider
challenge: A global payments provider faced regulator concerns over sanctions screening coverage after inconsistencies were identified between its transaction, customer, and counterparty screening pipelines.
solution: We completed a gap assessment against OFAC, UN, EU, and UK regimes; tuned matching algorithms and thresholds; and introduced a centralized fuzzy-name-matching service used by all screening pipelines. A remediation program back-tested historical activity against the corrected controls.
results: Screening coverage gaps were closed, false-positive volumes fell materially, and the provider closed its outstanding regulatory matter within the agreed remediation window.

title: CFT Program Uplift for Crypto Asset Exchange
challenge: A licensed crypto asset exchange needed to demonstrate a mature CFT program to satisfy conditions of its operating license, including robust travel-rule compliance and controls against terrorism-financing typologies specific to virtual assets.
solution: We designed and implemented an end-to-end CFT program covering VASP counterparty due diligence, travel-rule integration, blockchain analytics-driven typology detection, and a governance operating model aligned with FATF recommendation 15.
results: The license conditions were formally lifted, blockchain-analytics-driven investigations produced multiple actionable disclosures to authorities, and the exchange became a reference site for peers on CFT good practice.

title: Insider Fraud Detection Program for Insurance Group
challenge: An insurance group had identified a pattern of small-value insider fraud in claims handling but lacked the analytics and case-management tooling to detect it consistently across regions.
solution: We deployed link-analysis and anomaly-detection models on top of the claims data lake, and integrated the outputs into a unified case management workflow. Front-line training was refreshed to strengthen fraud awareness in claims and underwriting teams.
results: Detected insider fraud value rose sharply in the first year while overall investigation cycle time fell, and the group used its improved control environment as a proof-point in reinsurance negotiations.

title: AML/CFT Risk Appetite Framework for Challenger Bank
challenge: A rapidly scaling challenger bank lacked a documented AML/CFT risk appetite framework, making it difficult to demonstrate to regulators and investors that growth was being pursued within tolerable financial-crime risk boundaries.
solution: We authored a board-approved AML/CFT risk appetite framework with quantified thresholds, escalation triggers, and monthly monitoring metrics. The framework was embedded into product approval, market entry, and customer onboarding decisions.
results: The framework gave the board a defensible view of financial-crime risk versus growth ambition, was cited positively in the bank's next regulatory examination, and became a talking point in its Series C fundraising.
